# Buenos Aires performance venue research — Spectacles

Retrieved 7 November 2026. Scope: CABA, metropolitan Buenos Aires and La Plata, including the adjoining Gran La Plata municipalities. Names are preserved in the language and spelling published by each source.

## Coverage and limits

This file contains **4,621 consolidated archive venue records representing 4,632 named setlist.fm identities**, **372 additional registry entries classified for performance**, and **795 additional cultural-space candidates**. These are source records, not a certified count of distinct physical or currently operating venues. Historical names, rooms, stages and temporary outdoor performance locations can appear separately. Do not use the total as an active-venue count.

All **252 pages** of the **55 locality indexes listed below** were retrieved, yielding **4,690 unique provider IDs**. **62 generic Unknown Venue/Private Venue placeholders** are excluded from the venue catalog and preserved in a separate audit list. Retrieving every available page did not establish completeness: subsequent direct checks found important venues omitted from the retrieved index results, including Tecnópolis and the two Auditorios. This documents the retrieved pagination only; it does **not** prove that every venue in the whole region is listed. Unindexed/new venues, additional metro localities, relocations and source omissions remain possible.

Individual archive detail pages were checked for **892** named identities, including cached web copies. Other entries have index-verified names, locations and provider URLs, with unavailable fields left null. The provider returned HTTP 429 during further detail retrieval, so those requests were paused. Older cached facts are not a fresh verification of operating status. The city and province registries supply additional address evidence. Some source detail pages themselves omit addresses and coordinates.

Metropolitan scope for the provincial export is the 40 municipalities explicitly listed under methodology below. The archive locality list is the actual retrieval coverage, not a claim that those localities exhaust every settlement in those municipalities. Ensenada and Berisso are included with La Plata. The source does not establish a live-music program for every cultural center; these candidates are separate from the performance catalog.

## Project fields and interpretation

The schema was inspected in `backend/app/Models/Venue.php`, `backend/app/Http/Resources/VenueResource.php` and `backend/app/Models/VenueProviderId.php` in the existing Spectacles checkout before research. The following field mapping applies to every catalog entry.

| Project field | Meaning in this file |
| --- | --- |
| `name` | Canonical source display name; explicit site/branch qualifiers distinguish verified separate locations. |
| `address` | Published address, preserving intersections and ranges. |
| `street / house_number` | Explicit registry fields, or a conservative split of a simple source address. Ambiguous forms remain null. |
| `postal_code` | Only an explicitly published postal code. Never derived from a neighborhood or city. |
| `city / region` | Archive locality or explicitly published registry locality and jurisdiction. A provincial municipality is retained separately when locality is missing. |
| `country_code` | AR for every record. |
| `lat / lng` | Published venue points or unambiguous USIG address/intersection geocodes; the coordinate method is explicit in every entry. No city-center substitutes. |
| `timezone` | America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires for this geographic scope; assigned from location, not verified per venue. |
| `aliases` | Published aliases and confirmed consolidated source names. Branch-qualified headings retain the original institution name as an alias. [] means no aliases collected, not proof that none exist. |
| `image` | null for every record; no licensed venue image was collected. |
| `providerIds` | setlist_fm / venue / external ID from the source URL for archive entries. MusicBrainz place URLs also provide real place MBIDs when cited. BA Data, BASIC, EPOK, INAMU and directory references are research provenance; no app IDs are fabricated. |
| `UUID / timestamps` | Not generated. Those belong to the application when an authorized import occurs. |

For compactness, **country_code = AR**, **timezone = America/Argentina/Buenos_Aires** and **image = null** apply to every entry. Category, municipality, capacity, source dates, verification status and notes are research metadata; the current Venue resource has no dedicated fields for most of them. A source website is not an image. A source identity or index result alone is not proof of a concert, present-day opening status or an import-ready match.

## Sources and methodology

1. [Buenos Aires Data — Espacios culturales](https://data.buenosaires.gob.ar/dataset/espacios-culturales), Government of the City of Buenos Aires, Ministerio de Cultura. [Downloaded CSV](https://cdn.buenosaires.gob.ar/datosabiertos/datasets/ministerio-de-cultura/espacios-culturales/espacios-culturales.csv), 3,053 rows, SHA-256 `ecf9b636a30516cd3904280e04bddda98f7deaad1620a6f4898fd7b324961dde`. Portal metadata says updated 18 June 2026; that is not a per-venue verification date. License: [CC BY 2.5 Argentina](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.5/ar/). Names and factual fields have been selected and normalized as described here; attribution is retained. `fid` identifies a row in this particular snapshot, not a guaranteed permanent venue ID.

2. [BASIC — Sistema de Información Cultural de la Provincia de Buenos Aires](https://basic.gba.gob.ar/search), Instituto Cultural de la Provincia de Buenos Aires. Its public CSV export for Cultura comunitaria → Espacios culturales yielded 903 provincial records; 514 fall within the municipal scope. Export parameters: POST `/search`, `category=204`, `subcategory[]=261`, `sort=az-name`, `display=list`, `offset=0`, `export=1`. This is a search/export, with no record writes. SHA-256 `a3cdc04221b2398462a382428938a2a0ac44ce6be88d618d59bcd3704bcbae1a`. Row detail links retain the public record ID. BASIC permits reproduction with source attribution; its footer prohibits unauthorized commercial exploitation. No per-record update date was supplied in this export.

3. [setlist.fm venue archive](https://www.setlist.fm/venues). The individual venue links below are the citation for each archive identity. Each locality was enumerated through its public paginated venue list. Provider IDs, not name strings, deduplicate pagination. Venue detail facts are attributed to their individual page; no song lists, reviews or event histories were copied. Archive entries can exist without any submitted setlist.

4. Other sources investigated but not incorporated: SInCA national downloads (403/access failures), and an OpenStreetMap Overpass request (406). No records are claimed from failed requests.

City-registry selection: amphitheaters, theaters, live-music clubs, explicit secondary performance uses, cultural centers and milonga/peña categories. Unrelated libraries, bookstores, monuments, galleries and training spaces are excluded unless the same row explicitly identifies performance use. Provincial selection: independent theaters and cultural centers in the chosen municipalities. Generic cultural centers remain candidates until performance use is confirmed.

Provincial municipal scope: Almirante Brown, Avellaneda, Berazategui, Berisso, Brandsen, Campana, Cañuelas, Ensenada, Escobar, Esteban Echeverría, Exaltación de la Cruz, Ezeiza, Florencio Varela, General Las Heras, General Rodríguez, General San Martín, Hurlingham, Ituzaingó, José C. Paz, La Matanza, La Plata, Lanús, Lomas de Zamora, Luján, Malvinas Argentinas, Marcos Paz, Merlo, Moreno, Morón, Pilar, Presidente Perón, Quilmes, San Fernando, San Isidro, San Miguel, San Vicente, Tigre, Tres de Febrero, Vicente López, Zárate.

Joins use a unique exact normalized name or explicitly collected alias and exact locality, rejecting conflicting house numbers or incompatible street names. Case, accents and punctuation are ignored for matching only. These joins still require human review before import. Ambiguous name matches remain separate; address conflicts verified as alternate entrances or corrected against official venue pages are explicitly resolved in the ledger. Co-located rooms and branches are not merged merely for sharing an address. Confirmed aliases/historical names and duplicate registry rows are consolidated with all original IDs, source links and address variants retained in the resolution ledger. Names, country and timezone are not enough to establish venue identity. Source availability varies by record; nulls are intentional.

Address parsing only separates a trailing simple house number; it does not reinterpret La Plata numbered streets, infer postal codes or geocode missing coordinates. USIG address geocodes require a single geographic result in the source locality/jurisdiction and matching street identity and house number when one is explicit. An exact canonical street-name match is preferred over a nonexact/unofficial alias; otherwise multiple distinct points are rejected. Multiple identical points at a jurisdiction boundary can be treated as one point; different-point alternatives are rejected. These coordinates are approximate address/intersection positions, not independently surveyed entrances. Coordinate checks require complete numeric pairs within latitude (-35.5, -33.8) and longitude (-59.8, -57.0); this is a sanity check, not proof of a venue entrance. Category comes from a registry only; venue type is not guessed from a name.

5. [USIG official address normalizer/geocoder](https://servicios.usig.buenosaires.gob.ar/normalizar/), Gobierno de la Ciudad de Buenos Aires. [API documentation](https://usig.buenosaires.gob.ar/apis/). Exact request URLs are linked in each enriched entry. Address-derived positions are explicitly marked approximate and never overwrite a published venue point without an address correction. Responses with no point, wrong jurisdiction, conflicting house number or distinct alternatives remain unresolved.

## Enrichment and duplicate-resolution pass — 7 November 2026

The initial file had 5,859 source records, 1,576 addresses and 917 coordinate pairs. This pass consolidated **71 duplicate entries**, explicitly retained **16 separate branches/annexes**, checked further archive detail pages, corrected conflicting official venue addresses, and added vetted USIG coordinates. All source identities remain traceable; canonical record counts can decrease while factual coverage improves.

Measured against original source-record IDs, **445 previously missing addresses** and **712 previously missing coordinate pairs** are now filled. Net record totals also reflect consolidation, so they are not directly comparable to raw source-entry totals. Some coordinates are explicitly approximate geocodes; the method and evidence are included per venue.

## Other-source location research — 7 November 2026

This continuation starts from 1,597 addresses and 1,220 coordinate pairs in 5,789 canonical records. It fills **354 additional addresses** and **345 additional coordinate pairs**, without dropping or adding venue records. The earlier identity-resolution ledger remains in force.

Additional evidence searched:

- [Alternativa Teatral historical directory](https://www.alternativateatral.com.ar/teatros.asp?estado=todos&modalidad=t&pais=1): all 56 CABA pages (3,322 venue records) and all 36 Buenos Aires Province pages (2,144 venue records), including closed spaces. Public directory entries and their map positions were compared against existing names/aliases and the same locality. Province-wide rows are lookup evidence only; this catalog retains its existing geographic scope. Individual venue pages are cited in enriched entries.
- [Municipal independent-culture map](https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/cultura/cultura-independiente/mapa-de-espacios-culturales): 459 published map features, with object details checked for 21 candidate matches. Exact public EPOK object URLs and the map source are retained. Source modification dates can be historical and do not prove present-day operation.
- [INAMU Circuito Estable de Música en Vivo map](https://inamu.musica.ar/cemv/mapa): 44 public national venue records were inspected, including mapped locations within the research area. The official map page publishes these venue names, addresses and positions; contact-person data was not added to the catalog.
- [City cultural-center directory](https://buenosaires.gob.ar/cultura/conoce-los-centros-culturales) and [Abasto Cultural directory](https://buenosaires.gob.ar/gcaba_historico/cultura/abasto-cultural): 36 and 18 named location records, respectively.
- [MusicBrainz place search](https://musicbrainz.org/doc/MusicBrainz_API/Search/PlaceSearch): 95 place records with coordinates in the Buenos Aires bounding region were checked, including explicit place aliases. [Songkick Buenos Aires concert listings](https://www.songkick.com/metro-areas/32911-argentina-buenos-aires/venues): five public calendar pages yielded 219 event-location occurrences. Only compatible existing catalog identities were enriched; individual place/concert pages are cited in those entries.
- The complete 3,053-row BA Data cultural-space CSV was also checked, including bars, bookshops, libraries and museums that already appear as concert locations in this catalog. This supplies location evidence; it does not add unrelated institutions to the performance catalog or prove performance use for the separate cultural-space candidates.

Matching requires the same normalized source name/established alias and locality, or a distinctive name differing only in an explicit venue-type prefix/suffix. Existing house numbers and street identities must agree; mapped points must agree with existing venue coordinates. Multiple plausible locations are held for review. Published directory points repeated across unrelated addresses, missing-address placeholders, zero coordinates and points outside the relevant bounds are excluded.

Official address-geocode checks rejected **19 conflicting directory pins**. Where the address has a unique official street/house-number match, the approximate address-derived point is stored with an explicit conflict note and the discarded pin retained as evidence. This is not a surveyed venue entrance. Other unresolved name/location disagreements appear below.

## Important-venue additions and identity corrections — 7 November 2026

Added three canonical records with addresses and coordinates: Tecnópolis, its distinct covered Microestadio (Estadio del Bicentenario), and Auditorio Oeste. Added the current Auditorio Sur provider identity to the historical El Teatro Sur site, preserving its name history. Completed El Teatrito, Mandarine Park, Mandarine Tent and Teatro Argentino de La Plata; transferring the Malvinas registry point also completes its archive identity.

Four redundant catalog entries were removed: Luna Park registry duplicate, Malvinas Argentinas registry duplicate, Palacio Libertad archive duplicate, and CCK registry duplicate. All original IDs, source URLs, address variants and conflicting map points are retained in the canonical entries and resolution ledger. Park and covered stadium, and Mandarine Park and Tent, remain separate facilities. No stadium/microstadium pair was merged merely for sharing an address.

Coordinates include explicitly labeled approximate building/park points. The Mandarine pair shares a published combined-complex map point; individual stage/entrance pins are not established. The Microestadio organizer-booklet latitude required a documented southern-hemisphere sign correction. El Teatrito uses the independently corroborated Sarmiento 1752 address, with the archive's conflicting 777 retained in its note. Official and independent sources are linked beside each changed entry.

The catalog now contains **5,788 canonical records**, with **1,954 addresses** and **1,571 coordinate pairs**. Original pagination counts below remain the historical retrieved-index counts; four additional named archive identities were established by direct supplemental checks. This corrects important omissions without claiming region-wide completeness.

## Identity review groups

These remaining groups are not approved merges. A shared address can represent multiple stages, a parent institution and its room, independent businesses or successive occupants. In particular, Ferro stadium/microstadium, River stadium/microstadium, Hotel Bauen/its auditorium, and Sala Juan Bautista/Centro Cultural San Martín retain separate identities. Additional historical/name conflicts remain explicit instead of being silently collapsed.
